items.name: BlogConfig

```rust
    .with_theme_toggle("light", "dark", "dark")
    .build();
```

items.name: CopyPageButton
items.docs:
"Copy page" button for MDX documentation pages.

 Copies the page's raw Markdown source to the clipboard — the "copy page for
 LLMs" pattern. On success it swaps to a "Copied" state (check icon) for ~2
 seconds, then reverts.

 The Markdown is handed to the clipboard via `document::eval` argument
 passing (`eval.send`), never string-interpolated into the script, so
 backticks and quotes in the source can't break the JS.

 # Props

 - `content`: Raw Markdown source of the current page.

 # Stable public classes

 Carries `dk-copy-page` so theme presets can target the button.
# Props
*For details, see the props struct definition.*
- `content` : `String`

items.name: DocsLayout
items.docs:
Documentation layout shell.

 Renders the tab bar, sidebar, content area, search modal, and mobile drawer.
 The consumer wraps this in their own navbar via Dioxus route layouts.

 # Context requirements

 - `&'static DocsRegistry` — provided by consumer
 - `DocsContext` — provided by consumer

 # Props

 - `header`: Optional element to render inside the docs area header (e.g. branding + search button).
   If not provided, a default header with search button and hamburger is rendered.
 - `show_header`: Whether to render the internal header area (default header/custom header *and*
   tab bar). Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` when the consumer provides their own header
   and tab bar outside of `DocsLayout`.
 - `announcement_bar`: Optional element rendered at the very top, above `header`.
 - `sidebar_header`: Optional element rendered above the generated sidebar nav.
 - `sidebar_footer`: Optional element rendered below the generated sidebar nav
   (e.g. "Edit this page" links).
 - `footer`: Optional element rendered at the bottom of the layout (site-wide footer).
 - `variant`: Density preset (`Prose` default, `Reference` for denser API/reference docs).
 - `children`: The routed page content (from `Outlet` or explicit child).

 # Stable public classes

 `DocsLayout` tags its structural nodes with semver-stable `dk-*` classes so
 CSS overrides don't drift: `dk-root`, `dk-docs-root`, `dk-header`, `dk-shell`,
 `dk-sidebar`, `dk-main`, and slot wrappers like `dk-announcement-slot`.
# Props
*For details, see the props struct definition.*
- `header` : `Option<Element>`
- `show_header` : `bool`
- `announcement_bar` : `Option<Element>`
- `sidebar_header` : `Option<Element>`
- `sidebar_footer` : `Option<Element>`
- `footer` : `Option<Element>`
- `variant` : `DocsVariant`
- `children` : `Element`

items.name: DocsVariant
items.docs:
Density preset for the docs layout.

Consumers target the emitted class (`dk-variant-prose` or `dk-variant-reference`)
in their own CSS to further tweak the look. The shipped `theme.css` applies
width / type-scale differences out of the box.

members.name: Prose
members.docs: Default: wide margins, generous line-height, optimized for long-form prose.

members.name: Reference
members.docs: Tight: narrower article column, denser type, better for API/reference docs.

members.name: class

Injects SEO meta tags and document title for a single docs page (MDX or API endpoint).

 Reads `auto_meta` and `site_url` from `DocsContext`. When `auto_meta` is
 off, emits nothing. Otherwise pulls title/description from the registry —
 frontmatter for MDX pages, the OpenAPI operation's `summary`/`description`
 for API endpoint pages — and emits `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`,
 Open Graph, Twitter Card, and schema.org `TechArticle` JSON-LD tags.
 Canonical, `og:url`, the JSON-LD `@id`, and a `BreadcrumbList` are only
 emitted when `site_url` is also set.

items.name: use_theme_provider
items.docs:
Provide the `CurrentTheme` context and apply the persisted theme on mount.

Reads the stored preference from localStorage (falling back to the config's
default theme), sets `data-theme` on `<html>`, and keeps the returned signal
in sync. Called by `DocsLayout`/`BlogLayout`; call it yourself when you
render kit components (e.g. `ThemeToggle`) outside
those layouts, e.g. in a landing-page navbar.

items.name: ThemeToggle
items.docs:
Light/dark theme toggle button.

Reads theme configuration from `DocsRegistry` context and current theme from
the `CurrentTheme` context (provided by
`DocsLayout` or `use_theme_provider`).

Renders nothing if the registry has no `toggle_themes` configured.

items.name: ThemeConfig
items.docs:
Theme configuration for the documentation site.

Controls which DaisyUI theme(s) are applied and whether a toggle button is shown.

members.name: default_theme
members.docs: The default theme name (must match a DaisyUI theme defined in `tailwind.css`).

members.name: toggle_themes
members.docs: If set, enables a light/dark toggle button. Tuple is `(light_theme, dark_theme)`.

members.name: storage_key
members.docs: localStorage key used to persist the user's theme preference.

items.name: CodeThemeConfig
items.docs:
How rendered code blocks pick their syntax-highlighting theme.

Defaults to `CodeThemeConfig::Adaptive` with GitHub Light / Tokyo Night.

Only available with the `highlight` feature (default), which pulls in `dioxus-code`.

members.name: Fixed
members.docs: Always use this one theme, regardless of the site's light/dark state.

members.name: Adaptive
members.docs:
Pick `light` or `dark` to match the site theme.

When a light/dark toggle is configured (via `DocsConfig::with_theme_toggle`),
the choice tracks the active `data-theme` (not the OS `prefers-color-scheme`),
so code blocks stay in sync with the toggle. Without a toggle it falls back to
`prefers-color-scheme`.

items.name: DocsConfig
items.docs:
Builder for constructing a `DocsRegistry`.

# Example

```rust
let registry = DocsConfig::new(nav_json, content_map)
    .with_openapi("api-reference", spec_yaml)
    .with_default_path("getting-started/introduction")
    .build();
```

members.name: new
members.signature: pub fn new(nav_json: &str, content_map: HashMap<&'static str, &'static str>) -> Self
members.docs:
Create a new builder from a `_nav.json` string and a content map.

The content map is typically generated by `build.rs` using `include_str!()`.

members.name: with_openapi
members.signature: pub fn with_openapi(self, prefix: &str, yaml: &str) -> Self
members.docs:
Add an OpenAPI specification.

- `prefix`: The URL prefix for this spec's endpoints (e.g. "api-reference").
- `yaml`: The raw YAML string of the OpenAPI spec.

The `prefix` must correspond to a nav group in `_nav.json` whose `"group"` value
matches `Self::with_api_group_name` (defaults to `"API Reference"`). The library
dynamically injects API endpoints into that group's sidebar — do **not** list
individual operation paths in the `"pages"` array of `_nav.json`.

members.name: with_default_path
members.docs:
Set the default documentation path for redirects.

Defaults to the first page in the first nav group if not set.

members.name: with_api_group_name
members.docs:
Set the display name for the API Reference sidebar group.

Defaults to `"API Reference"`. The value must match a `"group"` in `_nav.json`
so the library knows where to inject the API endpoint sidebar entries.
See `Self::with_openapi` for details.

members.name: with_theme
members.docs:
Set a single theme (no toggle button).

The theme name must match a DaisyUI theme defined in the consumer's `tailwind.css`.

members.name: with_theme_toggle
members.signature: pub fn with_theme_toggle(self, light: &str, dark: &str, default: &str) -> Self
members.docs:
Enable a light/dark theme toggle.

- `light`: Name of the light DaisyUI theme.
- `dark`: Name of the dark DaisyUI theme.
- `default`: Which of the two to use on first visit (`light` or `dark`).

members.name: with_code_theme
members.signature: pub fn with_code_theme(self, theme: Theme) -> Self
members.docs:
Use a single, fixed syntax-highlighting theme for all code blocks.

Use this for single-theme sites (e.g. a dark-only app) so the code block
background matches the site instead of following the reader's OS setting.

Only available with the `highlight` feature (default), which pulls in `dioxus-code`.

members.name: with_code_themes
members.signature: pub fn with_code_themes(self, light: Theme, dark: Theme) -> Self
members.docs:
Use a light/dark pair of syntax themes for code blocks.

When a theme toggle is configured (see `Self::with_theme_toggle`), the active
choice tracks the toggle's `data-theme`; otherwise it follows the reader's OS
`prefers-color-scheme`. Defaults to GitHub Light / Tokyo Night when not set.

Only available with the `highlight` feature (default), which pulls in `dioxus-code`.

items.name: use_docs_providers
items.signature: pub fn use_docs_providers(registry: &'static DocsRegistry, docs_ctx: DocsContext) -> DocsProviders
items.docs:
One-call setup for all the context providers that `DocsLayout` and its
children expect.

Call this in your docs layout wrapper **before** rendering `DocsLayout`:

```rust
let providers = use_docs_providers(&*DOCS, docs_ctx);
// Use providers.search_open / providers.drawer_open in your header RSX
```

This replaces the manual calls to:
- `use_context_provider(|| registry)`
- `use_context_provider(|| docs_ctx)`
- `use_signal(|| false)` × 2 + `use_context_provider` for search_open / DrawerOpen

items.name: SearchEntry
items.docs:
A searchable entry in the documentation.

One entry per document *section* (split on h2–h4 headings): content before
the first heading is a page-level "intro" entry with an empty `heading` /
`anchor`, and each heading starts a new entry whose `anchor` deep-links to
the rendered heading id. OpenAPI operations are indexed as single page-level
entries. The `*_lower` fields are lowercased once at build time so search
never re-lowercases per keystroke.

members.name: path
members.docs: Content path of the owning page (e.g. "getting-started/introduction").

members.name: anchor
members.docs:
Anchor id of the section heading, empty for page-level / intro entries.
Matches the rendered heading `id` (`dioxus_mdx::slugify`).

members.name: title
members.docs: Page title (frontmatter title or humanised slug / API summary).

members.name: heading
members.docs: Section heading text, empty for page-level / intro entries.

members.name: description
members.docs: Page/operation description.

members.name: body
members.docs: Cleaned section body text used for matching and snippet extraction.

members.name: breadcrumb
members.docs: Sidebar breadcrumb (nav group, or API group + tag).

members.name: api_method
members.docs: HTTP method for API operation entries (drives the result badge).

Get the page title for the document `<head>`.

Resolves MDX frontmatter titles *and* OpenAPI operation pages (which are
not in `parsed_docs`): for an endpoint path it returns the operation
summary, falling back to a humanised slug. Branding/suffixes are left to
the caller.

members.name: get_page_description
members.docs:

Resolves MDX frontmatter descriptions *and* OpenAPI operation
descriptions, so endpoint pages ship a unique `<meta name="description">`
instead of falling through to a generic default.

members.docs:
Look up an API operation together with the spec that owns it.

Use this instead of pairing `Self::get_api_operation` with
`Self::get_first_api_spec` — with multiple registered specs, the
first spec is not necessarily the one the operation belongs to.

members.name: search_docs
members.docs:
Search documentation by query string.

Splits the query on whitespace and returns section-level entries whose
fields all match every term (multi-term AND), ranked title > heading >
description > body with a word-boundary bonus. See `crate::search`.

items.name: SeoRouter
items.docs:
Builder for the crawler-facing routes of a docs/blog site.

Generated routes:

| Route | Condition | Content |
|---|---|---|
| `<docs_path>/<page>.md` | docs | raw Markdown per doc page |
| `/llms.txt`, `/llms-full.txt` | docs | LLM-friendly docs index / full corpus |
| `/sitemap-docs.xml` | docs | docs sitemap |
| `<blog_path>/<slug>.md` | blog | raw Markdown per post |
| `<blog_path>/rss.xml` | blog | RSS feed |
| `/sitemap-blog.xml` | blog | blog sitemap |
| `/sitemap.xml` | always | sitemap index over the above |
| `/robots.txt` | always | allow-all incl. explicit AI-crawler entries |

- `site_title` / `site_description`: used in `llms.txt` headers and the RSS channel.

items.name: DOCS_KIT_CSS
items.docs:
Precompiled stylesheet covering every class the kit's components emit
(Tailwind utilities, DaisyUI dark/light themes, typography prose, and the
`--dk-*` token surface from `theme.css`).

Link it to run the kit without any Tailwind/Bun setup of your own:

```rust
rsx! {
    document::Stylesheet { href: dioxus_docs_kit::DOCS_KIT_CSS }
}
```

If your app already runs its own Tailwind build, skip this and use the
`safelist.html` approach from the README instead — the precompiled sheet
only contains the kit's classes, not yours.

Navigation bridge that decouples library components from the consumer's Route enum.

The consumer creates this in their docs layout wrapper and provides it via `use_context_provider`.

members.name: current_path
members.docs: Current docs page path (e.g. "getting-started/introduction").

members.name: base_path
members.docs: Base URL path for docs (e.g. "/docs").

members.name: navigate
members.docs: Callback to navigate to a docs page by content path.

members.name: site_url
members.docs:
Optional full site URL (e.g. `https://example.com`). Used as the canonical
host for emitted `<link rel="canonical">` and `og:url` tags. Independent
of `auto_meta` — set it whenever you want kit helpers
(sitemap generation, canonical URLs) to know the public origin, even if
you suppress automatic meta emission.

members.name: auto_meta
members.docs:
When true, the kit emits per-page `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`,
Open Graph and Twitter Card tags from frontmatter. Set to `false` if your
app manages its own `<head>` (e.g. brand-specific OG images, structured
data) and the kit's emissions would conflict. Title and description tags
always emit when this is on; canonical and `og:url` only emit when
`site_url` is also set.

members.name: markdown_alternate
members.docs:
When true, `DocsPageMeta` emits a
`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` pointing at the page's raw
Markdown source (`<base_path>/<path>.md`), a discoverability hint for AI
crawlers and "view as Markdown" tooling. Enable this only if your server
actually serves those `.md` URLs (see `server::SeoRouter` behind the
`server` feature). Emitted only for MDX pages (OpenAPI endpoint pages
have no Markdown source), and only when `auto_meta`
is also on.

members.name: new
members.signature: pub fn new(current_path: impl Into<ReadSignal<String>>, base_path: impl Into<String>, navigate: Callback<String>) -> Self
members.docs:
Create a context from the three required fields.

The meta fields default to `site_url: None`, `auto_meta: true`,
`markdown_alternate: false`; override them with the `with_*` setters.
Prefer this over a struct literal — new fields get sensible defaults
here instead of breaking your build.

members.docs:
Optional full site URL (e.g. `https://example.com`). Used as the canonical
host for emitted `<link rel="canonical">`, `og:url`, and JSON-LD URLs.
Independent of `auto_meta` — set it whenever you want
kit helpers (sitemap/RSS, canonical URLs) to know the public origin, even
if you suppress automatic meta emission.

members.name: auto_meta
members.docs:
When true, the kit emits per-page `<title>`, `<meta name="description">`,
Open Graph, Twitter Card, and Article JSON-LD tags from frontmatter. Set
to `false` if your app manages its own `<head>` (e.g. brand-specific OG
images, structured data) and the kit's emissions would conflict. Title
and description tags always emit when this is on; canonical, `og:url`,
and JSON-LD `@id` only emit when `site_url` is also set.

members.name: markdown_alternate
members.docs:

`<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">` pointing at the post's raw
Markdown source (`<base_path>/<slug>.md`), a discoverability hint for AI
crawlers and "view as Markdown" tooling. Enable this only if your server
actually serves those `.md` URLs (see `server::SeoRouter` behind the
`server` feature). Emitted only when `auto_meta` is
also on.

items.name: doc_content_map
items.docs:
Generates a `doc_content_map()` function that returns a
`HashMap<&'static str, &'static str>` from the build-script output.

Place this at module level in your `main.rs`:

```rust
dioxus_docs_kit::doc_content_map!();
```

Requires `dioxus-docs-kit-build` in `[build-dependencies]` and a `build.rs`
that calls `dioxus_docs_kit_build::generate_content_map("docs/_nav.json")`.
